The Amanatides–Woo algorithm efficiently enumerates the uniform grid cells intersected by a ray in front-to-back order by jumping exactly from one grid boundary to the next, avoiding the pitfalls of naïve ray marching such as missing thin cells, redundant work, and arbitrary step sizes [S1, unofficial, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the Amanatides–Woo algorithm efficiently enumerates uniform grid cells intersected by a ray in front-to-back order by jumping from boundary to boundary, avoiding pitfalls of naïve ray marching (missing thin cells, redundant work, arbitrary step sizes). Source [S1] explicitly confirms all these points: it introduces the algorithm by John Amanatides and Andrew Woo, describes the mechanism of jumping exactly from one grid boundary to the next, lists the specific pitfalls of naïve ray marching that are avoided, and confirms the front-to-back enumeration order. Source [S2] provides a practical implementation that aligns with this logic, further supporting the description of the algorithm's behavior.
